name: MO-06
label: Safe R

key_factors: District's R+19 partisan lean makes it one of the most Republican seats in Missouri
Stigall's roughly seven-to-one fundraising edge over Smead
Prediction markets price the Republican near 96 percent

model.rationale: The open seat sits in an R+19 district where Republican Chris Stigall has out-raised Democrat Josh Smead about seven to one, and markets price the Republican near 96 percent. Even with a Democratic-leaning national environment, a Republican hold in the mid-teens is the clear expectation.
model.watch: A late surge of Democratic outside spending or an unusually large national wave could narrow the margin, though an outright upset would still require a historic shift.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Sam Graves (R) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Missouri's sixth district, anchored in the state's rural northwest, is among the most Republican-leaning seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly nineteen points toward the GOP. Sam Graves's retirement creates an open seat, but Republican nominee Chris Stigall enters the general election with a large financial advantage, having raised more than one million dollars to about 146 thousand for Democrat Josh Smead. A Libertarian candidate is also on the ballot.

No public polls or expert ratings cover the race, but prediction markets price the Republican at roughly 96 percent to win. The national environment leans Democratic this cycle, which could narrow the margin somewhat, yet the district's fundamentals make a Democratic victory a long shot. The expectation is a comfortable Republican hold in the mid-teens.
